scope: Offline postprocessing diagnostic on a prior experimental Split candidate, not production or a new native observation
method: Use application-collected hits in face order to associate endpoints first with current-face corners strictly within 0.001, then with first-seen points within the inferred Float32-derived 0.0001 radius. Apply the resulting Float32 aliases to already-triangulated experimental output and drop facets with duplicate corners; compare unordered Float32 facet multisets and summed triangle areas with ten retained native outputs.

results.threeRemainingCases: The below, at and above small-radius controls each retain one additional nondegenerate triangle after mapping. Their areas are approximately 0.000045, 0.000050 and 0.000055 square mm, respectively.
results.areaSums: Each source and mapped result sums to 0.5 square mm; native outputs sum to 0.4999549999993178, 0.4999500000012631 and 0.4999449999995704 square mm, respectively. These are triangle-area sums, not an independent overlap or boundary analysis.

limitations: The diagnostic uses a prior isolated experimental candidate and applies associations after triangulation, unlike the hypothesized native order. It does not test the current production candidate.
The cases were known before this model was selected; no independent scaled native result was available. Output winding, ownership, topology, GUI and MCP are not compared.
The diagnostic test asserts the number of cases and retains measured differences; its passing status is not a native equivalence assertion.

Dropping an additional nonzero facet would remove area in these controls. The static reason for the native output and the general rule remain unresolved; no application change is justified by this observation alone.
